ts transforms¶

transforms holds the element-wise and windowed operations that turn a series into another series of the same length: changes (diff, returns, log_returns), shifts (lag, lead), rolling and expanding statistics, exponentially weighted statistics, a rolling z-score, and gap filling. They are the building blocks the models of the other families expect their input to have gone through.

All of them take a one-dimensional Series and return a Series of the same length. Positions where a statistic is not yet defined (before a window has filled, or because a value needed does not exist) hold NaN, so the output always lines up with the input observation by observation. A NaN inside a window makes the statistic of that window NaN.

The Surface¶

Entity

What it gives you

diff

The first difference of a series: each observation minus the one periods positions earlier

ema

The exponential moving average of a series; the same computation as ewm_mean

ewm_mean

The exponentially weighted moving average of a series

ewm_std

The exponentially weighted standard deviation of a series

expanding_mean

The mean of all observations up to each position

expanding_std

The standard deviation of all observations up to each position

fill_gaps

Replaces missing values (NaN) in a series by carrying values forward or backward, or by a constant

lag

The series shifted later in time: position t holds the observation from periods steps earlier

lead

The series shifted earlier in time: position t holds the observation from periods steps later

log_returns

The logarithmic return of a series: the natural log of the ratio of an observation to the one periods earlier

resample

Aggregates a time-indexed series into coarser time bins, such as days, weeks or months

returns

The simple return of a series: the relative change over periods observations

rolling_max

The largest value in each window of window consecutive observations

rolling_mean

The mean of each window of window consecutive observations

rolling_min

The smallest value in each window of window consecutive observations

rolling_std

The standard deviation of each window of window consecutive observations

rolling_sum

The sum of each window of window consecutive observations

rolling_var

The variance of each window of window consecutive observations

zscore_rolling

The rolling z-score: each observation minus the window mean, divided by the window standard deviation

How To Call It¶

Compute the changes, the lagged values and a three-period rolling mean of one series and print them side by side.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}

int main() {
  const Series x = pluss::make_series({10.0, 12.0, 11.0, 15.0, 14.0, 18.0, 17.0}, f64);
  show("x", x);
  show("diff", ts::diff(x));
  show("lag", ts::lag(x));
  show("rolling mean", ts::rolling_mean(x, 3, 3));
}

Output

x               10.0000  12.0000  11.0000  15.0000  14.0000  18.0000  17.0000
diff                nan   2.0000  -1.0000   4.0000  -1.0000   4.0000  -1.0000
lag                 nan  10.0000  12.0000  11.0000  15.0000  14.0000  18.0000
rolling mean        nan      nan  11.0000  12.6667  13.3333  15.6667  16.3333
